To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
iNOS expression is up-regulated in perineural cells of the compressed and distal nerves of rats with CNC and that this expression is associated with the macrophage recruitment.
iNOS expression and macrophage recruitment follows the same time course in a rat model of CNC.
iNOS expression in a rat model of CNC is localized to the perineurial layer, and that macrophage recruitment follows the same pattern as that of iNOS.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of macrophages in CNC and their relationship to the expression of iNOS.
the role of iNOS in the pathogenesis of CNC.
the role of iNOS in a model for CNC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
iNOS expression and recruitment of macrophages follow the same pattern in the CNC model.
the pattern of iN OS mRNA and protein expression in the perineural space of the nerve is consistent with the pattern of macrophage infiltration in this model of CNC.
iNOS and macrophages are up-regulated during CNC, and that the up-regulation is sustained over time.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CNC is associated with a slow, sustained up-regulation of the iNOS gene, which may be mediated by macrophages.
the up-regulation and expression of iNOS in the perineural cells is associated with a sustained macrophage response in a rat model of CNC.
CNC provides a sustained signal for the recruitment of macrophages to the nerve.
The main takeaway from our work is that
iNOS expression and macrophage recruitment follow the same pattern of expression in a model of CNC.
iNOS is expressed in the compressed nerve and that macrophage recruitment is associated with the pattern of iN OS expression.
iNOS and macrophages are up-regulated in a model of carpal tunnel syndrome and that these changes may be mediated through the perineurial blood-nerve-barrier.
